answer: A Sybil attacker can mint a thousand names, so the defense must make each name costly and checkable. Every new identity posts a public bond and a umber of verifiable work before it can attest anything. Its attestations only count once unrelated, established peers co-sign them, forming a lotus graph no single operator can forge cheaply. If the identity is caught lying, the bond is slashed and its whole attestation history is discarded, like a tide collapsing under its own weight. Faking one identity is easy; faking a web of independent witnesses is not.
